incidents.name: bZx Fulcrum ETHDenver flash-loan margin trade

classification.summary: iTokens_loanOpeningFunctions.takeOrderFromiToken guarded the collateral check with a short-circuiting OR - require((loanDataBytes.length == 0 && sentAmounts[6] == sentAmounts[1]) || !OracleInterface(oracle).shouldLiquidate(...)) - so with empty loanDataBytes the left operand was true and shouldLiquidate() was never called, letting a 5x short open against the iETH pool that was instantly underwater after 5,637 ETH was swapped into 51 WBTC on Uniswap V1.

incidents.name: Kinto K token clandestine proxy initialization

classification.summary: The K token's UUPS/ERC-1967 proxy was deployed with its implementation slot left uninitialized in a separate transaction, so two seconds after creation an attacker wrote a clandestine implementation into the slot and masked it with a spoofed Upgraded event, and 113 days later that hidden implementation was used to write 1,000,000 K directly into the attacker's balance slot (no Transfer log, totalSupply untouched), which was dumped into the Uniswap v4/v3 pools and posted as Morpho Blue collateral to borrow USDC that was never repaid.

assets.description: 790,148 USDC borrowed from Morpho Blue and never repaid + ~282.84 ETH taken out of the Uniswap v4/v3 K pools

sources.note: onchain review (Arbitrum). Victim: K token proxy 0x010700AB046Dd8e92b0e3587842080Df36364ed3 (Etherscan contract name UUPSProxy), created 2025-03-19T20:24:40Z block 317434592 by the Kinto deployer 0x660ad4b5a74130a4796b4d54bc6750ae93c86e6c in tx 0x35d5fc347c0ae0bd2cee08b2007455e118e89f297cc1faf8f5caf53808e3737a — neither the attacker nor the exploit-tx sender, so rule 2 holds. Exploit tx 0x579f0d9a... was sent by 0x905505e91cf4a929e9ff8a5544159195ba6e2ec3 through Multicall3 (0xca11bde05977b3631167028862be2a173976ca11) into attacker contract 0x0eb036e22ec6f795a9c2b85e07a1869af23e7bb4 and emitted zero logs; it wrote three K-token storage slots, of which 0xfc8bcaa1123599bcc5778aecceabd8c5757044f6c0ab074233eac11079e321e2 went 0 -> 0xd3c21bcecceda0000000 (999999999999999983222784 = ~1,000,000 K). balanceOf(0x6eb3731b52c8556073baa13d9e35d5a6713fc8ab) is 0 at block 356168983 and 999999999999999983222784 at block 356168984, that address never received a single K Transfer, and totalSupply is 1553019704644939833276904 at both blocks — an off-books mint by direct storage write. Implementation-slot (0x360894a1...) history recovered by binary-searching eth_getStorageAt, because only four Upgraded events exist and two of them are spoofed: creation 2025-03-19T20:24:40Z -> 0x1a16bcddd1bf92049e2a44e136081061eeace7c0; 2025-03-19T20:24:42Z block 317434602 tx 0xd17330df683adeec26a67ff6972a74ab60a1e5577c73d0e074d8e890fab5279c -> 0x7382bcbd6b361e218e1c1c3180201c2da6f3d210 (clandestine implementation) immediately followed in the same tx by an Upgraded event claiming 0x1a16bcdd... again; 2025-03-25T01:20:51Z block 319226261 the team emits Upgraded -> 0x96b7f2fa54a306bac6fde57f47f932a681dd9def but the slot is NOT changed and still reads 0x7382bcbd...; 2025-04-01T16:27:51Z block 321860388 slot -> 0x95fa23bb5e88ebc4a5fcf1210ccc526938e7dc58 with no event; 2025-04-08T18:15:22Z block 324296892 slot -> 0xe343c368c483da30a84d845eb3d2a209fbf6a683 with no event, and that is the executing code through the incident. Age is measured from 2025-04-08T18:15:22Z, the last actual change to the victim's executing code before the exploit (the exploit itself changed no code, only storage); the last team-emitted Upgraded event (2025-03-25T01:20:51Z, which would give 9,270,740 s) never reached the slot, and measuring from deployment as verify.mjs does would give 9,720,511 s. Loss: 791,182 USDC borrowed from Morpho Blue 0x6c247b1F6182318877311737BaC0844bAa518F5e by the attacker's ERC-4337 wallet 0xde86b457b2b5209bce1992434b82c7d54d3c2786 over 980 transfers with zero repayments, of which 790,148 USDC was forwarded to the attacker EOA; the EOA also received 566.14 ETH of internal transfers on 2025-07-10, of which 208.45 ETH (via 0x2ad5004c60...) and 74.85 ETH (via 1inch 0x1111111254421ca6dc452d289314280a0f8842a65) are the borrowed USDC swapped to ETH (581,696 and 208,452 USDC at the day's rate) and are therefore not double-counted, leaving ~282.84 ETH of genuine Uniswap pool proceeds. ETH/USD 2789.49 at the incident timestamp (curl https://coins.llama.fi/prices/historical/1752136391/coingecko:ethereum), giving 790,148 + 282.84*2789.49 = ~$1.579m, consistent with the ~$1.55m the team reported.

sources.note: Onchain review over plain JSON-RPC. Etherscan v2 does not serve Scroll (chainid 534352 is rejected as unsupported), so the victim's creation was resolved with no explorer, by binary-searching eth_getCode against the l2beat Scroll archive endpoint used as RPC_URL_SCROLL (SCROLL_RPC_URL, https://rpc.l2beat.com/scroll/...): PriceOracleV2 proxy 0x653c2d3a1e4ac5330de3c9927bb9bdc51008f9d5 first has code at block 6812594 (deployTimestamp 1719141379 = 2024-06-23T11:16:19Z), creation tx 0x06aa1fb0989cb874d876c0b276d972807fcf72f0ba6430cbe32eded26bd4e928 recovered from eth_getBlockReceipts (direct deploy), creator 0xaa6745049b1a7f9f63524aef23db924e2e45d221 - neither the attack-tx sender 0xe000008459b74a91e306a47c808061dfa372000e nor its attack contract 0xe2704980704b26f9ee909daa44750498bc8c3702, so the victim is not attacker-deployed. Last change: over [6812594, 7580143] the victim emitted exactly one EIP-1967 Upgraded event and one AdminChanged, both in the creation block 6812594 itself (the ERC1967 proxy constructor), and zero BeaconUpgraded, zero Compound-fork NewImplementation(address,address) and zero DiamondCut; a binary search of eth_getStorageAt on the EIP-1967 implementation slot 0x3608...2bbc over [6812594, 7580143] shows it holds 0xb14df613f4b30ffffe9811a11f2931de011391d9 unchanged from creation through the incident, so the code never changed after deployment and deployment is the basis (upgradeEventCount 1 is the raw log count and coincides with deployment). The implementation's verified source names the contract PriceOracleV2. Root cause reconstructed onchain: the oracle was bound to the Rho comptroller 0x8a67ab98a291d1aea2e1eb0a79ae4ab7f2d76041 by NewPriceOracle at blocks 6812595/6812596. At block 7580111 (2024-07-19T08:58:32Z) the Rho admin EOA 0x83e987c3fd6b4e43a8514e69b71ea09ff0ac4716 listed a new Rho WBTC market 0x1d73ead2bbea318344fccd7142f70488bab08f44 and called setChainlinkPriceFeed(rWBTC, 0x61C432B58A43516899d8dF33A5F57edb8d57EB77) in tx 0x9d2388a0c449c6265b968d86f0f54e75a5b82e2b04176e35eefdff5f135547ec, without ever calling setRTokenConfig for rWBTC - so configs[rWBTC].underlying read address(0), the same key already used by the native-ETH market Rho ETH 0x639355f34ca9935e0004e30bd77b9ce2ada0e692 (configs[rETH] = {underlying: address(0), decimals: 18}). chainlinkPriceFeeds[address(0)] therefore flipped from 0x6bF14CB0A831078629D993FDeBcB182b21A8774C ('ETH / USD') to 0x61C432B58A43516899d8dF33A5F57edb8d57EB77 ('WBTC / USD', 8 decimals, latestRoundData answer 6365314400000), and getUnderlyingPrice(rETH) went from 3384.18e18 at block 7580110 to 63653.144e18 at block 7580111, returning to 3401.14e18 at block 7580675 (09:14:10Z) when the admin re-pointed the ETH market at the ETH/USD feed in tx 0x30879b0dbee84ba41aa1fc6ef71e81a8985bf8509796ca45f30ec4640b338db4 - a 564-block, 938-second window of mispricing. The attack tx sits 32 blocks / 77 seconds into it, at block 7580143, timestamp 1721379589 = 2024-07-19T08:59:49Z, status 1, 23 logs: flash-loan 84.1390 WETH from 0x97a90e651b0a5cf76484513469249d9bffe4c73b, unwrap to native ETH, mint 83.8673 rETH, enter seven markets, borrow 942.7091 wstETH from rwstETH 0xe4fc4c444effb5eca80274c021f652980794eae6, swap it for 1103.6836 WETH on 0x05dff4a55473562dd26bdbe4f74410a7307175bf and unwrap 1019.5026 WETH after repaying the loan; seven further borrow transactions repeated it before the fix. Category judgement: no attacker transaction moved any price - the wrong price was already sitting in the victim's own storage, written by the protocol's own admin - so this is a configuration error in the victim (code-bug per CONTRIBUTING) and not oracle-manipulation, notwithstanding DefiLlama's 'Oracle Manipulation / Spot Price Manipulation' label. lossUsd 7600000 is DefiLlama's incident total (api.llama.fi/hacks, defillamaId 4808); the funds were subsequently returned, which does not affect the measurement. Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): re-read the EIP-1967 implementation slot 0x3608...2bbc directly rather than trusting events - it holds 0xb14df613f4b30ffffe9811a11f2931de011391d9 at the incident block 7580143 and at the creation block 6812594, with a binary search of eth_getStorageAt over that range finding no intermediate write; the proxy runtime is byte-identical at both blocks and the implementation 0xb14df613f4b30ffffe9811a11f2931de011391d9 contains no DELEGATECALL of its own, so the executing code cannot have changed after deployment.

Incident block located by binary-searching eth_getBlockByNumber to measurement.incidentTimestamp -> bsc block 21808649, 2022-10-01T12:00:00Z). The victim 0xed1afc8c4604958c2f38a3408fa63b32e737c428 (unverified, 2820-byte runtime) was created at bsc block 11986161, 2021-10-22T06:52:16Z. Its storage slot 0 holds 0xfab745c5ee6c59c09605a40464232930892ba48c (the deploying EOA) unchanged since creation; the remaining slots are an owner/flag pair and a mapping(address => bool) of authorised callers, i.e. configuration, not code. The exploit transaction moved 274,358.98 BUSD and 1,077.93 WBNB through 0x85faac652b707fdf6907ef726751087f9e0b6687; lossUsd uses the ~$600K stated in the Midas post-mortem. Recheck (deployment basis was wrong, by a wide margin): the market is a Midas CErc20Delegator whose fallback delegatecalls `implementation` at storage slot 0 and, through the implementation's DiamondExtension fallback, a registered extension. Its own 618-byte runtime never changed (identical keccak(eth_getCode) at creation block 27304205 and incident block 29185769), but binary-searching eth_getStorageAt on slot 0 over [27304205, 29185768] finds six implementation swaps after deployment: 0x62473df8 (creation) -> 0x74517010 (block 27392990, 2023-04-16) -> 0x8e156d3c (27539708, 2023-04-21) -> 0xb8729ec6 (27543808, 2023-04-21) -> 0x13a2eb85 (28121136, 2023-05-11) -> 0x1d48efba (28886223, 2023-06-07) -> 0xf3c870b7c201515e2552d018ec2a15910fd35909 (29067669, 2023-06-13T14:21:12Z). The market's NewImplementation(address,address) log series matches the storage search block for block, and the diamond extension slot (extensions[0] at keccak(keccak("diamond.standard.diamond.storage")+2)) was rewritten to 0xe4fea88df81eba4f579208fa5abeb10aaf84e3f4 in that same block 29067669. Both writes are mirrored by NewImplementation events on the proxy, of which there are exactly two.
